classification.difficultyReason: Translate square areas into side lengths and choose coordinates to express the two gradients, proving both directions of the perpendicularity condition. Then connect three right triangles through repeated Pythagoras to obtain the largest square's area.

content.prompt: Consider trapezium $ABDE$ shown below. Point $C$ lies on $BD$. The areas of the four smaller squares shown are $a^2$, $b^2$, $c^2$ and $d^2$.

spec.description: Connected external squares on AB, BC, CD, DE and AE. Preserve B–C–D order and triangle ACE. Internal drawing coordinates specify schematic proportions only, not additional numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: AB and DE are vertical; BD is horizontal. The four smaller squares have areas a², b², c² and d². The largest square has side AE.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied point and area labels remain visible; no derived lengths, coordinate axes or right-angle mark at C are supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $\angle ACE=90^\circ$ if and only if $ad=bc$.

answer.short:
$\angle ACE=90^\circ$ if and only if $ad=bc$.

The gradients of $AC$ and $CE$ are $-\frac{a}{b}$ and $\frac{d}{c}$; their product is $-1$ exactly when $ad=bc$.
answer.worked:
Take $B=(0,0)$ with $BD$ along the $x$-axis and $AB$ along the $y$-axis. The square areas give $A=(0,a)$, $C=(b,0)$ and $E=(b+c,d)$.

$$\begin{align*}m_{AC}&=\frac{0-a}{b-0}\\m_{AC}&=-\frac{a}{b}\\m_{CE}&=\frac{d-0}{(b+c)-b}\\m_{CE}&=\frac{d}{c}\\m_{AC}m_{CE}&=-\frac{ad}{bc}\end{align*}$$

Thus $AC$ and $CE$ are perpendicular exactly when $-\frac{ad}{(bc)}=-1$, which is equivalent to $ad=bc$. Therefore $\angle ACE=90^\circ$ if and only if $ad=bc$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $\angle ACE=90^\circ$, then find the area of the largest square shown.

answer.worked:
The square side lengths give $AB=a$, $BC=b$, $CD=c$ and $DE=d$. By Pythagoras in the right-angled triangles $ABC$ and $CDE$,

$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=a^2+b^2\\CE^2&=c^2+d^2\end{align*}$$

Since $\angle ACE=90^\circ$,

$$\begin{align*}AE^2&=AC^2+CE^2\\AE^2&=a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2\end{align*}$$

The largest square has side $AE$, so its area is $a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2$.
